verdicts.title: Demand
verdicts.question: Is use of NEAR Intents still growing?
verdicts.rule: Supported if the last 90 days of volume are at least 1.0x the 90 days before; contradicted below 0.8x.
verdicts.reading: NEAR Intents settled $12.60B in the last 90 days against $6.94B in the 90 days before.
verdicts.against: Volume is DefiLlama's series, not rebuilt from chain logs here, and part of the flow now settles on a private path that public indexers cannot see.

verdicts.title: Income against the security bill
verdicts.question: How much of what NEAR pays for security comes back to holders?
verdicts.rule: Supported if buybacks plus gas burn cover at least 50% of NEAR minted over 30 days; contradicted below 20%.
verdicts.reading: The chain minted 89,520 NEAR a day. Captured Intents revenue bought 14,530 and gas burned 804.
verdicts.against: Coverage is counted in NEAR while revenue is earned in dollars, so the same revenue covers less when the price rises. Bought NEAR is held, not burned.

verdicts.title: Does the money arrive
verdicts.question: Do the revenue wallets on chain hold what the revenue series says they received?
verdicts.rule: Supported if the three revenue wallets gained at least 90% of the NEAR the series implies over the window; contradicted below 75%.
verdicts.reading: From 2026-10-24 to 2026-11-23 the three wallets gained 457,652 NEAR; the series implies 416,809.
verdicts.against: Nothing in code locks these wallets. A multisig can move the balance, so this measures a policy that has been kept so far, not a rule.

verdicts.title: Security after the cut
verdicts.question: Does a smaller security budget still price an attack well above what the chain settles?
verdicts.rule: Supported if one third of all stake costs at least 2x the value held in NEAR Intents at spot; contradicted below 1x.
verdicts.reading: One third of the 596,286,007 NEAR at stake is worth $637.1M at spot, against $164.6M held in NEAR Intents.
verdicts.against: Spot value is not an attack cost: buying that much would move the price up, and a price fall shrinks the margin without any change in stake.

verdicts.title: Validator set after the cut
verdicts.question: After issuance falls to 1.6%, how much stake sits with validators whose fee income still pays for the machine?
verdicts.rule: Supported if at least 90% of stake sits with validators whose commission income covers $500 a month at the post-cut rate; contradicted below 67%.
verdicts.reading: 83 of 345 validators clear the bar after the cut (96 today); they hold 88.9% of stake.
verdicts.against: The $500 a month cost is an assumption, and commission is a lower bound on operator income because it leaves out rewards on the operator's own stake.

verdicts.title: Who could halt the chain
verdicts.question: How many validators would have to act together to hold a third of stake?
verdicts.rule: Supported at 10 or more validators; contradicted below 7.
verdicts.reading: The 10 largest of 345 validators hold more than a third of stake; the ten largest hold 36.0%.
verdicts.against: Validator accounts are not owners. Several pools can belong to one operator, so the true number is this or lower.

verdicts.title: The holder who stakes
verdicts.question: Does a staker's share of all NEAR still grow after the cut?
verdicts.rule: Supported if the real staking yield after the cut is above 0%; contradicted below -0.5%.
verdicts.reading: Staking pays 3.68% a year today and 2.35% after the cut; net of supply growth that is 1.18% and 0.77%.
verdicts.against: This holds the staked share fixed. If lower rewards make holders unstake, the yield per staked NEAR rises and the stake securing the chain falls.

stance.label: Subsidised
stance.summary: 5 of 7 tests supported, 1 contradicted. NEAR earns back 17.1% of what it pays for security; the HSP-029 cut alone would lift that to 26.8%.
